To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The Hopfield network is a valid model for a large associative memory, (2) The Hopfield model is a valid model with only two-body interactions, (3) The Hopfield dynamics is the dynamics of a microscopic model that minimizes a Lyapunov energy function, (4) The dynamics of the microscopic model can be derived from a variational principle that minimizes an entropy function.
(i) The dynamics of the Hopfield model can be described in terms of an underlying microscopic theory that involves additional (hidden) dynamical variables and two-body interactions.

(i) the Hopfield network is not a biologically plausible theory, (ii) the model proposed in the "Hopfield Networks Is All You Need" is a biologically plausible version of the Hopfield network, but not a biologically realistic one, and (iii) the microscopic theory proposed in this paper is a biologically realistic version of the model proposed in "Hopfield networks is all you need".

a microscopic theory of associative memory and its relation to the macroscopic (written in terms the original variables) models that have been proposed in the literature.

the Hopfield model is a valid description of a more microscopic model with additional (hidden) degrees of freedom, which can be viewed as a model of associative memory in the brain.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Hopfield networks can be viewed as the mean field theory of a more microscopic model that has additional (non-biological) hidden neurons, and that these additional neurons are not necessary for the associative recall process, but they are needed to make the model biologically plausible.
we have provided a microscopic theory for large associative memories that is a valid model for Hopfield networks and their generalizations.

our theory is a more microscopic description of the model presented in  "Hopfield Networks Is All You Need" and it is also a generalization of the models discussed in "Dense Associative Memory with Multi-body Interactions" and "Dense Associativity in a Recurrent Neural Network with Two-Body Interactions" papers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of our microscopic model is the most fundamental and that other models can be derived from it by integrating out certain variables.
the dynamics of the hidden neurons can be used to construct the energy function for a large associative memory, without having to explicitly know the form of the latter.
one can obtain a large associative memory with only two-body interactions by adding a small number of additional neurons to the system.
